name: Competition Strategy
description: A competition study worksheet using the public Watson BJJ strategy map and the rules adopted by your event.
summary: Turn a broad technique collection into a position-by-position plan for a specific tournament.
overview: Watson BJJ’s Gameplan / Strategy Map distinguishes general development from tournament preparation: the competition version lists the game you plan to use at that event. Its separate top and bottom sections make missing answers visible. Use the map to organize familiar options, then check their scoring and legality against your event’s rules.

guide.display_title: Competition Strategy: Map Your Intended Game

fits: You have several favorite techniques but no written plan for where a match might leave you.
consider_alternative_if: If the main uncertainty is what scored, Competition Scoring Strategy is the more focused starting point.

includes: Separate planning spaces for standing, guard, pins, turtle and leg-attack situations.
A distinction between options you intend to use now and material you want to develop later.
limits: The worksheet is a planning aid, not evidence that a listed sequence will succeed.
Its technical examples are not a universal game plan or a division-specific legality list.

start_here.title: Compare your planned route with your last match
start_here.task: Use the blank map on pages 2–3. Enter your intended standing choice and the position you expect next using techniques you already study. Trace one recent match through the corresponding boxes and circle the first box where your plan had no entry. Put a familiar option there for discussion with your coach; keep a separate list for techniques still to learn.
start_here.section: Gameplan / Strategy Map: Competition Prep, page 1; worksheet, pages 2–3.

sources.title: Gameplan / Strategy Map — Watson BJJ
sources.note: Read the three-page worksheet: general development and competition preparation use the same positional map differently. The competition instructions focus on the game intended for the next tournament.
sources.viewed_range: Pages 1–3, particularly Competition Prep and the blank position sections

flashcards.question: How does the Watson BJJ strategy map distinguish a tournament plan from a general development plan?
flashcards.answer: The tournament version selects the game intended for the next event; general development can also include techniques the student wants to add with further practice.
flashcards.answer_line: Select the game for this event
